question:
Square \(EFGH\) is inside square \(ABCD\) so that each side of \(EFGH\) can be extended to pass through a vertex of \(ABCD.\) Square \(ABCD\) has side length \(\sqrt{50},\) \(E\) is between \(B\) and \(H,\) and \(BE = 1.\) What is the area of the inner square \(EFGH?\)

[Figure 1](figures/2005_AMC_12A_Q07_question_fig1.svg)
solution:
The right triangles beside the outer sides \(AB\) and \(BC\) have equal hypotenuses. Proving them congruent will transfer the known length \(BE=1\) to triangle \(AHB\).

[Figure 1](figures/2005_AMC_12A_Q07_question_fig1.svg)

The side extensions put \(A,H,G\), \(B,E,H\), and \(C,F,E\) on straight lines. Since adjacent sides of the inner square are perpendicular, triangles \(AHB\) and \(BEC\) are right at \(H\) and \(E\), respectively.

Let \(\theta=\angle ABH\). In right triangle \(AHB\), we have \(\angle HAB=90^\circ-\theta\). Also, \(BE\) lies along \(BH\) inside the outer square's right angle \(ABC\), so \(\angle EBC=90^\circ-\theta\). Thus the triangles have two corresponding angles equal and equal hypotenuses \(AB=BC\). They are congruent by AAS, giving \(AH=BE=1\).

Now the Pythagorean theorem in triangle \(AHB\) gives
\[
BH^2=AB^2-AH^2=50-1=49.
\]
Because \(BH\) is a positive length, \(BH=7\). Since \(E\) is between \(B\) and \(H\),
\[
EH=BH-BE=7-1=6.
\]
Therefore the inner square has area \(6^2=\boxed{36}\), choice \(\mathrm{C}\).
